subject: Dedicated capacity node-mix recommendation for Valence AI (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)
messages:

Cc: ops@valence.ai

Subject: Valence workload + ask: recommended node mix for Dedicated

Hi Mateo / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Attached is our updated workload profile (valence-workload-profile-v2.xlsx) — two things we need help with by next Tuesday:

1) A recommended Dedicated node mix (how many H100 / A100 / L4 nodes) for our initial commit (~200k monthly active requests, mostly chat + embedding) given the profile.
2) A short risk note: what falls back if H100 capacity is constrained (latency vs quality tradeoffs).

High-level details:
- Primary model family: a mix of long-context LLMs (32k-ish) for docs workflows and smaller 8k-16k models for chat.
- Peak concurrency: 240 concurrent sessions, median request size ~600 tokens, p95 tokens ~3.2k.
- Embeddings: batch-processed and real-time small embedding calls (~2k qps burst).

We prefer predictable latency for end-user chat (p90 < 400ms) but are cost-conscious. Happy to set up a short call to walk through.

Cheers,
Priya Sharma
Head of ML Ops, Valence AI

Thanks Priya — got the profile and the ask. Looping in Priyom for sizing sims and Kimberly for commercial/capacity options.

Quick notes from my read:
- Long-context models (32k) will be memory-bound; H100s (80GB/80GB HB) enable the largest context with good throughput but at higher $/hour.
- A100 (40GB) can cover mid-length sequences more cheaply if you tile/strip long inputs or use sequence-splitting.
- L4 is excellent for low-cost, high-concurrency embedding and small chat models — good candidate for burst capacity and background embed jobs.

Request to Priyom: please run a focused sim across three mixes (H100-heavy, A100-hybrid, L4-augment) and include tail-latency (p95/p99) and monthly unit cost estimates. Include assumptions about quantization (int8) and batching behavior.

Priya — can we do a 30-minute call Monday 6/14 to review the sims? Kimberly, I left the open commercial questions to you (commit levels, burst windows).

Best,
Mateo
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Valence workload + ask: recommended node mix for Dedicated

Hi all — ran the sims and attached a short CSV and cost PDF (gpu-mix-sim-v1.csv, cost-estimates-q2.pdf). Summary below (assumptions at the bottom).

Executive summary (short):
- Option A — H100-dominant (60 H100 + 8 A100 + 12 L4): best p95/p99 latency for 32k contexts and high-concurrency chat; cost = baseline X (high).
- Option B — Hybrid (30 H100 + 30 A100 + 20 L4): balanced — H100 handles hot long-context paths, A100 handles medium-length chat with tiling, L4 takes embeddings and low-priority chat; cost = baseline ~0.72X.
- Option C — A100-forward (8 H100 + 68 A100 + 24 L4): lower capex/commit cost, needs aggressive splitting for long-context; risk of increased tail latency and more orchestration complexity; cost = baseline ~0.53X.

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Memory headroom: H100 (80GB) comfortably supports 32k tokens with int8 quantization for model families that compile well. A100 (40GB) will require either model sharding (more complex) or sequence chunking which increases end-to-end latency.
- Latency profile: H100 gives best single-request latency for long-context since it avoids cross-device syncs. A100 hybrid with intelligent routing can hit p90 <400ms but p99 tails can be 2-3x higher for big contexts unless you reserve extra headroom.
- Embeddings: L4 is cost-efficient and supports very high QPS for small models; recommend offloading real-time embedding to L4 and keep H100/A100 for generative models.
- Fallbacks: If H100 is constrained, automatic routing to A100 with degraded latency but similar quality is the pragmatic fallback. For quality-sensitive long-context, the platform can fall back to a reduced-context sync (e.g., 8k window) with a warning to the app.

Sizing rationale: used the provided profile, p95 concurrency = 160, peak bursts up to 240. Sim details: average request ~600 tokens, p95 ~3200 tokens, embedding qps spikes accounted for in L4 cluster simulations.

Attachments: gpu-mix-sim-v1.csv (sim output snapshot), cost-estimates-q2.pdf (cost model with reserved vs burst pricing).

Assumptions (short):
- Quantization: int8 available for selected models; some degradation risk for 32k variants, model-specific validation required.
- Batching: continuous batching window 8-12ms assumed for chat to balance latency/cost.
- Autoscaling: reserved minimum set to 75% of baseline, burst to 125% using L4 pool.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Pick an option (A/B/C) as starting commit.
2) Run a 7-day pilot with mixed traffic to validate p99s and quantization quality.
3) Lock in reserved pricing for the chosen commit and add a small burst L4 pool for overnight embedding jobs.

Happy to walk through numbers on the call.

--
Priyom Das
Applied ML / Inference Sizing, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@valence.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valence workload + ask: recommended node mix for Dedicated

Priya — thanks for the profile and thanks Priyom for the sims. From the commercial side:

- For a first reserved commit, we typically recommend starting with the Hybrid (Option B) — it gives predictable latency while keeping cost efficiency. For Valence's numbers, a 12-month commitment at Option B volumes yields a ~21% effective discount vs on-demand.
- We can structure the contract so H100 headroom is guaranteed at the reserved level, A100 is part of the baseline, and L4 is available as burstable capacity (with a small reserved minimum to ensure embed reliability).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on reserved nodes; latency SLOs can be included in the playbook with remediation credits tied to p99 violations.

Attachments: reserved-pricing-valence.pdf (pricing tiers and proposed monthly commit).

Commercial questions for you Priya:
1) Will you be comfortable with a 12-month reserved commit with the Option B volumes?
2) Are there internal procurement constraints (PO cycle, security review timeline) we should map against the pilot?

If yes, we can fast-track legal and schedule a kickoff. Mateo — can you and Priyom lead the pilot runbook? I can coordinate contracts and billing.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachment: reserved-pricing-valence.pdf (6 pages)

From: Priya Sharma <priya@valence.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valence workload + ask: recommended node mix for Dedicated

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful. Quick answers:
- We want to proceed with Option B (Hybrid) as the initial committed mix. 12 months is OK but we need a 60-day exit/checkpoint tied to observed p99 and quality metrics.
- Procurement: standard PO cycle, expect 3-4 weeks for procurement + security review. We can start a 7-day pilot next week under an MSA addendum if needed.

One follow-up: what precisely happens if H100 capacity is degraded regionally? You mentioned fallback to A100 and reduced-context mode — how automated is that routing, and can we opt into conservative routing (send long-context only to H100 until certain headroom)?

Would appreciate a short paragraph we can put in our internal ops runbook describing the fallback behavior (automated routing rules + manual escalation).

Cheers,
Priya
